result: Dynasore and Pitstop-2 effectively block both slow and fast endocytosis at the calyx of Held synapse. Bath-applied Dynasore (100 μM) and Pitstop-2 (25 μM) almost completely blocked slow endocytosis (29 fF/s) and significantly inhibited fast endocytosis (reducing rates from ~350 fF/s to ~150 fF/s), with potency comparable to direct intracellular loading of dynamin-1 PRD peptide.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm this finding, stating 'The data presented make a compelling case for fast endocytosis as necessary for rapid site clearance and vesicle recruitment to active zones.' The pharmacological validation of endocytic blockers is accepted without critique.

result: Endocytic blockers enhance synaptic depression at the calyx of Held in a frequency-dependent manner. At 100 Hz stimulation, both Dynasore and Pitstop-2 markedly enhanced synaptic depression starting at 10 ms (2nd stimulation), increasing steady-state STD from 58% to 75%. The enhancement was significant at high frequencies (100 Hz) but minimal at lower frequencies (10 Hz), with effects restricted to the early epoch of transmission.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly support this finding, noting 'The data reveal an unexpected, fast role for local site clearance in counteracting synaptic depression.' The frequency-dependent nature of the effect is highlighted as a key observation without challenge.

result: Endocytic blockers did not prolong recovery from short-term depression at post-hearing calyces under physiological conditions. Contrary to previous reports, recovery from STD was not prolonged and was even significantly accelerated at both fast and slow components after 100 Hz stimulation.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding without critique. The contrast with previous literature is acknowledged in the manuscript and not questioned by reviewers, suggesting acceptance of this unexpected result under the specific physiological conditions tested.

result: Scaffold protein inhibitors (ML141 and Latrunculin-B) enhance synaptic depression at the calyx of Held without affecting endocytosis. These inhibitors markedly enhanced STD at both 10 Hz and 100 Hz stimulation (increasing STD magnitude 1.4 times), with effects that were stronger and frequency-independent compared to endocytic blockers, despite not blocking endocytosis itself.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly highlight this as 'the most interesting finding,' stating that 'acute disturbance of the synaptic actin network leads to a marked frequency-dependent enhancement of synaptic depression in the Calyx.' The dissociation from endocytosis effects is accepted.

result: Endocytosis and scaffold machinery operate through complementary rather than additive mechanisms at fast synapses. Co-application experiments revealed that fast endocytosis clears vesicle residues while scaffold machinery simultaneously mobilizes and replenishes vesicles, together maintaining high-fidelity neurotransmission up to 500 Hz at the calyx of Held.
evaluation: Reviewers affirm this mechanistic interpretation, stating the study 'reveals some interesting differences between a fast synapse (Calyx of Held) tuned to reliably transmit at several 100 Hz and a more slow hippocampal CA1 synapse,' implicitly accepting the proposed complementary mechanisms.

result: Endocytic blockers attenuate synaptic facilitation at hippocampal CA1 synapses. Under physiological conditions, hippocampal synapses showed facilitatory short-term plasticity. Both Dynasore and Pitstop-2 significantly attenuated this facilitation, with Dynasore also unexpectedly enhancing basal EPSC amplitude.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding as part of the comparative analysis between synapse types. The observation is included in their summary of 'interesting differences between a fast synapse...and a more slow hippocampal CA1 synapse' without critique.

result: Scaffold protein inhibitors have no effect at hippocampal CA1 synapses. ML141 and Latrunculin-B had no effect on EPSC facilitation at hippocampal synapses, suggesting the actin-dependent scaffold machinery operates predominantly at fast synapses and is non-functional at relatively slow synapses.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly highlight this as 'the most interesting finding,' emphasizing 'This striking difference between both preparations' regarding the differential effects of actin network perturbation. The synapse-specific nature of scaffold protein function is accepted.

result: Endocytosis-dependent release-site clearance is a universal phenomenon supporting vesicle replenishment at both fast and slow synapses. The mechanism operates at both calyx of Held and hippocampal CA1 synapses, suggesting it is a conserved feature across mammalian central synapses.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this conclusion, noting the study is 'a comprehensive and comparative study, which reveals some interesting differences' between synapse types, implicitly affirming the universal nature of endocytic site clearance while acknowledging synapse-specific differences in scaffold mechanisms.

result: Quantitative analysis demonstrates that fast endocytosis can fully compensate initial synaptic depression during high-frequency transmission. The reduction in endocytic rate (200 fF/s) corresponds to 2.54 vesicles/ms, which translates to an estimated EPSC amplitude reduction of ~1.4 nA in 10 ms, closely matching the observed amplitude difference at the 2nd EPSC under 100 Hz stimulation.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge this quantitative analysis. Their statement that the data 'make a compelling case for fast endocytosis as necessary for rapid site clearance and vesicle recruitment' implicitly accepts the quantitative estimates supporting this mechanism.

result: Slow endocytosis is unlikely to contribute to millisecond-order site clearance but may play a housekeeping role. The rate of slow endocytosis (29 fF/s) is ~10 times slower than fast endocytosis (250-350 fF/s), suggesting it serves to prevent accumulation of vesicular membrane from spontaneous exocytosis rather than supporting rapid replenishment.
evaluation: Reviewers do not question this interpretation. Their focus on 'fast endocytosis as necessary for rapid site clearance' implicitly accepts the distinction between fast and slow endocytosis roles without challenging the proposed housekeeping function of slow endocytosis.

result: Enhanced synaptic depression by endocytic blockers is caused by presynaptic mechanisms. Since glutamate does not desensitize or saturate postsynaptic receptors at post-hearing calyces, and results were unchanged in the presence of kynurenic acid, the effects are attributed to presynaptic site clearance mechanisms.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this mechanistic interpretation without challenge. Their statement about 'rapid site clearance and vesicle recruitment to active zones' focuses on presynaptic mechanisms, consistent with the authors' interpretation.

result: Physiological calcium concentration (1.3 mM) reveals robust STD-counteracting function of F-actin without Ca2+-dependent recovery. Latrunculin A and B were equipotent at 1.3 mM Ca2+, and the Latrunculin-sensitive fast recovery component (CDR) was absent at physiological calcium, suggesting CDR operates only during excessive Ca2+ entry.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these findings. The emphasis on 'physiologically optimized conditions' in the review comments suggests acceptance of results obtained under physiological calcium concentrations.

result: The physiological role of vesicle acidification and ultra-fast endocytosis (UFE) in hippocampal synaptic transmission remains unclear. Vesicle acidification blockers had no effect on short-term synaptic efficacy, and despite Latrunculin-A blocking UFE in culture, its equipotency with Latrunculin-B at calyceal synapses suggests UFE's role is uncertain.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these negative findings or interpretations. The acceptance of the overall study as 'comprehensive' suggests these observations are viewed as appropriately cautious conclusions about mechanisms not clearly demonstrated under the experimental conditions.
